neighbours.label: England's Glorious Revolution of 1688: William of Orange and Mary taking the throne, James II's flight to France, and the settlement that followed (with or without the year); other revolutions and other uses of 'Orange' stay low
fire: When William of Orange landed in Devon, King James's army melted away.
James II threw the Great Seal into the Thames as he fled London.
Whig historians praised the Glorious Revolution as bloodless.
William and Mary were crowned together in Westminster Abbey.
After the Glorious Revolution, Parliament gained real power over the crown.
The Catholic king James II lost his throne to his Protestant daughter and her Dutch husband.
Jacobites spent decades trying to undo the revolution of 1688.
John Locke returned from exile in Holland once William had taken the throne.
quiet: When Napoleon landed in the south of France, the king's army melted away.
King Charles I was beheaded outside the Banqueting House in London.
Marxist historians praised the Russian Revolution as inevitable.
Elizabeth II was crowned alone in Westminster Abbey.
After the French Revolution, the National Assembly abolished feudal dues.
The farmer grew orange trees on his small plot in Florida.
Loyalists spent decades trying to undo the American Revolution.
John Locke wrote about property and the rights of citizens.
neighbours.notes: Found as a 'single year' pole for 1688 in the year atlas. Probes: 'William of Orange took the English throne in the Glorious Revolution' 1.02 with no year, 'Parliament offered the throne to William and Mary' 0.53, 'James II fled to France' 0.46, the Bill of Rights of 1689 0.26; 'The old mill opened in 1688' 0.36 (it reads the year too), 1688 as a count 0.001; the French Revolution 0.14, the American Revolution 0.03, the Orange Order 0.02, orange juice 0.00.
